All 17 importers of routes.py import the router or app, not these handler internals, so nothing breaks for them.

Schema and persistence: no database change. The TOML config gains a persisted `general.shutdown_drain_timeout` key on the next settings save. Before this diff, saves already wrote the model default 60.0 for this key, because `_settings_to_dict` serializes the whole validated model. The on-disk shape is unchanged; only the source of the value changes.

Validation chain is tighter (safe change): safe_float rejects non-finite values (validation.py:203-223) and clamps to [1, 3600]. The model then re-checks with ge=1.0 and allow_inf_nan=False. inf, nan, -inf, 0 and negative values from the form all end up finite and at least 1.0. I found no bypass.

Staged change: the config value has no runtime consumer yet. scheduler.py:58-81 reads only TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT, once at import. The 75-03 plan does the wiring. Because settings.html has no drain input yet (75-02 Task 2 is pending), the UI does not expose the field on any path, so a missing consumer is not a defect at this step.

Tests: test_web.py:694 (the settings page shows the drain input) will keep failing until 75-02 Task 2 adds the template input. That is expected under the red-first TDD sequence (commit ce567d3). test_web.py:737 and :773 (round trip, and the floor clamp at 0.5 -> 1.0) should pass with this diff.
Performance: none. One float parse per settings POST.
Main follow-up: the model has no upper bound but the form caps at 3600 (impact-1). Decide on one range before the template's max=3600 ships, or a TOML value above 3600 will block form submission.
Verdict: shippable as one step of the staged phase. No blocking issues. The bound mismatch (impact-1) is worth resolving within phase 75.

The user then cannot save any setting until they lower the drain value by hand.
